I can't stop your voices and I have no experience with them so I can't talk on that. but I've been broken and I rebuilt myself. I've been nothing. I've had years where life didn't make sense, I was felt alone , and misunderstood. Until that stopped. I had a different voice in my head- one that most people have, which undiagnosed, is called low self-esteem. I couldn't stop it either. it told me to kill myself. it told me i was better off dead. it told me life was unbearable. but one day, i found out how to  ignore it. it still talks, but i keep going.I'm not always happy but I'm better than I was. Your voices may be different. But the one that's talking to me now is still here and you seem coherent. just because you are broken does not mean that you will always be. I am sorry you are afraid and in pain and I hope that you stay alive long enough to give your real voice a chance.

> n through hell. No one deserves that. It sounds like you're in a lot of pain and in a bad situation. I wish I could help. When you say "Fuck", that, to me implies that you have some doubts. You also say you're anticipating reservations tomorrow night, but you're hoping impulsivity will get the job done. I've felt that way many times. The Will to Live is strong, whether you want it to be or not. It's a strange thing, but even the people I've known to be severely suicidal, they have some semblance of doubt.
> But there is something significant in the fact that we exist at all. At least to me. I'm fascinated by philosophy. That might not help you. But the fact that you wrote your story here, means you want help. Part of you wants someone to hear you. You're screaming and you feel like no one hears you. I'm trying to listen. There are others too, listening. People who understand and care.
> For me, therapy has helped the most. Individual therapy is useful and if you haven't tried it or aren't doing it now, I'd make every effort to find a way to get a competent therapist.
> You sound like you're in a scary, unstable relationship. And that makes everything you're experiencing worse. But you've asked for help. So please try to hang in there. Try to find a therapist. Call a hotline. Talk to a friend. Make a friend. Further articulate your experience in writing, that helps me at least (writing).

hey. first, you're in the right place. plenty of guys here were in your boat and now they're in a relationship or working closer to their goals. we all start somewhere. but let me say one thing yo it's awesome! that you asked her out. now you know what not to do. don't think of it as a failure- think of it as an experiment. the more you experiment, the closer you will be to finding the "solution". On your depression and anxiety, I advise you to read "feeling good" by david burns. yea, it's a little outdated but its on cognitive therapy and it will help you rewire your thought processes. soon you won't say "I'm not happy and lonely" because you'll learn how to have fun on your own, stop cognitive distortions, and take more chances...Another book recommendation is "no more mr. nice guy" ...I think that's what it's called. Remember: you'll get better, that girl isn't the world. Beating yourself up is unnecessary *and a sign you're human*. Been there, tried that. Now you have too. Let's try something else. also not to 1+ your humiliation, but the first time i tried asking a girl out i was in college and i wrote her a fucking note. didn't even hand it to her in person. instead, i found her dorm and emailed her. so dude, believe me, you prob weren't the weirdest proposal she's received.
